docs: Test runner table. DATA, not code: adding a runner means adding an entry
here. A user override at <config dir>/test_runners.json is merged in front
of this file.
Per runner:
language       informational label
detect_paths   runner applies if any of these exist in the project
detect_content [{file, contains}] - applies if the file contains the text
workdir        subdirectory to run from (default: project root). The
first entry whose directory exists is used.
binary         same resolution as linters.json (name / project_paths /
python_env), plus:
run_as_module  launch as '<interpreter> -m <module>'
instead of the console script, using the
interpreter next to the resolved binary.
Needed for pytest: the console script
omits the working directory from
sys.path, so an uninstalled pkg/ + tests/
project fails to collect.
args           argv after the binary. Substitutions:
{report} temp file the runner writes results to
{root}   project root
target_args    appended when the caller asks for a specific test target
parser         'junit_xml'     standard JUnit XML report (most precise)
'go_json'       `go test -json` newline-delimited events
'jest_json'     `jest --json` report file
'cargo_text'    `cargo test` human output, panics included
'unittest_text' `unittest -v` output, tracebacks included
'summary'       counts only, from human output (last resort;
it cannot name what failed, so prefer any
parser above when adding a runner)
summary_regex  for parser=summary: named groups passed/failed/skipped
timeout_s      hard limit for the run
Runners are ordered by the key name; detection decides what actually runs.
